message.content:
Here’s a quick rundown of the most common “tools” (websites, mobile apps, APIs, and even some offline options) you can use to book flights:

| Category | Tool / Service | What it offers | Typical use‑case |
|----------|----------------|----------------|-----------------|
| **Online travel agencies (OTAs)** | **Expedia** | Full flight + hotel + car bundle, loyalty points | Great for package deals |
| | **Kayak** | Price comparison across many OTAs | Quick price‑check, flexible dates |
| | **Priceline** | “Name Your Own Price” and Express Deals | Last‑minute bargains |
| | **Orbitz** | Similar to Expedia, often has promo codes | US‑centric deals |
| | **Hotwire** | Discounted “opaque” fares | Budget travelers |
| | **Travelocity** | Easy booking, often bundled | Family trips |
| | **CheapOair** | Focus on low‑fare airlines | One‑way or round‑trip |
| | **Momondo** | Aggressive price‑comparison, includes low‑cost carriers | International flights |
| | **Google Flights** | Fast search, price graph, calendar view | Quick research, price alerts |
| | **Skyscanner** | Multi‑city, flexible dates, price alerts | Global search, multi‑stop |
| | **Hopper** | Predictive pricing, “book now or wait” | Mobile‑first, price prediction |
| | **Trip.com** | Strong in Asia, often cheaper fares | Asian routes |
| | **Airbnb Experiences** | Not a flight tool, but can bundle flights & local experiences | Experiential travel |
| **Airline‑direct booking** | **Delta, United, American, Southwest, Ryanair, EasyJet, Air France, Lufthansa, Emirates, Qantas, etc.** | Direct seat selection, frequent‑flyer miles | Loyalty, seat control |
| **API / SDK** | **Amadeus for Developers** | Flight search, booking, availability, pricing | Integrate into your own app |
| | **Sabre APIs** | Comprehensive travel data, booking, inventory | Enterprise‑level solutions |
| | **Travelport (Apollo)** | Global distribution system (GDS) | Travel agencies, corporate booking |
| | **Skyscanner API** | Search, price alerts, flight data | Build custom search tools |
| | **Google Flights API** (unofficial) | Search & price data | Research, analytics |
| | **FlightAware API** | Real‑time flight status, delays | Tracking, customer support |
| | **OpenSky Network API** | Real‑time flight data, ADS‑B | Aviation enthusiasts, data science |
| **Mobile Apps** | **Airbnb, Booking.com, Skyscanner, Hopper, Kayak, Google Flights** | All‑in‑one travel planning | On‑the‑go booking |
| | **FlightRadar24** | Live flight tracking | Check flight status |
| | **TripIt** | Organize itineraries | Post‑booking management |
| **Offline / Traditional** | **Travel agencies** | Personal assistance, complex itineraries | Multi‑destination, corporate |
| | **Corporate travel portals** | Company‑specific booking tools | Business travel |
| | **Phone booking** | Call airline or OTA | Accessibility, special requests |

### How to choose

1. **Price vs. convenience** – OTAs and price‑comparison sites are great for finding the cheapest fare, but airline‑direct booking gives you more control over seat selection and loyalty miles.
2. **Special needs** – If you need a multi‑city itinerary, a GDS (Sabre, Amadeus) or a dedicated OTA that supports complex routing is best.
3. **Mobile vs. desktop** – Apps like Hopper or Skyscanner are optimized for quick searches on the go, while full‑feature sites like Expedia or Kayak are better for detailed planning.
4. **API integration** – If you’re building a travel app or want to embed flight search into a website, Amadeus, Sabre, or Skyscanner APIs are the go‑to choices.

Feel free to let me know if you’d like deeper details on any particular platform or how to integrate a specific API!
